post.description: Starts a goal's curriculum (skill graph, plan and course outlines) or, for an explain question, its quick explanation again, such as after a start failed. A run already going is joined, and only what is missing is written. POST /goals starts it the first time. Stream GET /generations/{generationId}/events for live steps: a curriculum reports `understandGoal`, `readExamNotice` (only while research reads a class test's own material before its skill graph), `readNotice` (only while research reads a stored exam notice again with newer reading instructions before the skill graph), `buildSkillGraph`, `saveSkills`, `preparePlacement` (placement's questions start being written, by a run of their own that this stream doesn't follow: GET /goals/{goalId}/placement asks each once it's written), `createPlan`, `outlineCourses`, `prepareFirstLessons`, then `goalReady`, or `workflowError` when the plan couldn't be built; an explanation `classifyQuestion`, `findExplanation`, `writeExplanation` (completed once the explanation can be read), then `explanationReady` once its course to go further is linked. A run that finds another run already writing the goal reports `joinRunningGoal` or `joinRunningExplanation` with that run's id as `entityId`: follow that run's events instead. Starting a goal whose plan is already built again with a newer `researchId` reconciles the plan with that research, which counts as small AI help: a refusal is `SLOW_DOWN` or `USAGE_LIMIT_REACHED` (403 asks a guest to sign up, 402 a free learner to upgrade or come back, 429 Plus to slow down).

Starts a Library course as the learner's goal, with nothing to type or confirm: a learn goal on the course (a language goal for a language course) whose plan is built from the course's outline right away, its level bands as phases, starting at `chapterId` when one is sent (the chapters before it are left out). Onboarding (GET /goals/{goalId}/onboarding) then asks only the level and the learner's time, and places them (a language's level test); a chapter start skips the level and placement. A new goal's run starts writing ahead what its plan needs (placement's questions, the first lessons); follow it through the onboarding's `generationId`, or POST /goals/{goalId}/generations when it didn't start. A course nobody outlined yet gets its plan from that run. It counts against the plan's goal limits (429 GOAL_LIMIT_REACHED or SLOW_DOWN); the learner's active goal already on the course comes back instead (200). Published public courses, and the learner's own private ones. Guests can start one.

get.description: A Library lesson ready to play: its screens in order (hook, explanations, worked examples, checks, typed and spoken answers, activities, the summary and language exercises) with image URLs. The content is the same for everyone and includes the answers, so the app can give feedback at once. The screens load only with a session, a guest's included (POST /guests): without one, a written lesson returns its outline with `status: "sessionRequired"`, so lessons can't be scraped. While the content is being written, returns the outline with `status: "notGenerated"`. Reading screens is rate-limited per learner, and per network for guests: too many lessons in a short time is `SLOW_DOWN` (429, read it again after `Retry-After`). A private lesson is only visible to its owner.

post.description: Claims a pending or failed question and returns one grounded answer as an AI SDK UI message stream, whatever the question is about (a lesson, chapter, plan or mock). `lessonId` in the question routes is a Library lesson. A first question about a lesson screen that someone already asked there streams the saved shared answer right away, without counting against the allowance or reading memory. Otherwise the answer counts against the learner's tutor allowance (403 asks a guest to sign up, 402 a free learner to upgrade, 429 to slow down or come back after the limit resets, with `SLOW_DOWN` or `USAGE_LIMIT_REACHED` and details), and reads the learner's memory. Its `finish` event comes once the answer is saved, so the answer is done and the learner can ask again; a `data-memory` part may follow with what the exchange changed in memory (each change's `action`, `fact` and `previous` with `id` and `statement`), to show and undo with `POST /v1/me/memory/change-reversals`. In a goal's conversation with the buddy, a `data-plan-change` part carries the plan change the answer proposed (a `PlanChange` waiting for the learner's OK) as soon as it's saved; the question's `planChange` holds it too. A `data-plan-changes-replaced` part follows it with the `ids` of earlier proposals it replaced because it changes the same thing (their status is now `replaced`). When the buddy only acted (a plan change or an app tool) and wrote nothing, the answer is a short confirmation of what it put under it.

correctAnswer.description: Null in checkpoints until they end

trap.description: In a trap drill, the trap the question set, named after the answer

workedSteps.description: A math problem's worked steps with the numbers it showed; empty for other questions and in checkpoints until they end

bestStreak.description: The most right answers in a row on new or due material

ceremony.description: At most one ceremony per session

finished.description: Every block is done or skipped. False right after "Stop for today": the rest of the session waits to be picked up

netScore.description: Right minus wrong on the session's net-scored questions (Cebraspe practice and swipe capsules); null without them

title.description: The course's title, which onboarding opens with

SuggestedGoal.description: A course the learner was taking before goals existed, offered as a goal to plan: "Continue Physics? Build a plan in 1 minute"

exam.description: An exam goal's final stretch, day before, exam day or "How did it go?"; null otherwise

dateEstimated.description: The date is the likely day of an exam whose notice isn't out yet

daysLeft.description: Whole days until the goal's date; null for a goal without one

guardianInvite.description: A learner under 18 with an account and no guardian invited yet: offer to invite one (POST /v1/me/guardian-links), with "Not now" (POST /v1/me/guardian-invite-dismissals)

insight.description: At most one insight from recent sessions, until it's answered

lessonStatus.description: Where each lesson of the day's learn blocks stands; a stop still being written says so. Follow one with `/v1/library/lessons/{lessonId}/readiness`

planChange.description: The plan change to answer on Today: the newest proposal waiting for an OK, or an automatic change of the last day (a rebalance, missed days, a test-out) until it's marked seen. Answer it with PATCH /v1/goals/{goalId}/plan/changes/{changeId}

behind.description: For missedDays: falling behind made the plan cover less of its goal by its date. Offer that daily time, keeping the time with less depth, or choosing where to focus. Null when the date isn't at risk

canFocus.description: The plan has more than one area to choose where to focus

currentMinutes.description: The learner's daily time, which covers coveredAfter

dailyMinutes.description: The daily time to offer: the one that covers the whole goal in depth again (fullDepth), else the most time a day; null when the learner already gives it

measure.description: A share of the exam's questions and points, or of the goal

canUndo.description: True while the plan is still as the change left it

days.description: For missedDays: the earlier days that left lessons, now first

kind.description: edited, testedOut, missedDays, estimateUpdated or resumed; keep unknown kinds

lessonsSkipped.description: Plan items a test-out skipped, the same count as its result

officialDate.description: The exam day the notice officially sets, when the change moves the goal's date off it. Say it with the change and label applying it as keeping the learner's own date anyway. Null otherwise

source.description: The address of the notice that sets it

reason.description: The sentence to show as written when an AI or a proposal wrote it; null when the client says it from kind, operations and effect, as for every change read from the learner's words (`source: planEdit`, the buddy's or the plan page's), so its card says what it does, never what was asked

seen.description: The learner said "Got it" to it, so the plan no longer shows it

source.description: learner, planEdit, tutor, system, or the part that proposed it

status.description: proposed waits for the learner's answer; replaced: a newer change about the same thing (the time, the date, the focus, the exam's notice) replaced it before they answered, so it can't be applied

todaySession.description: For a change the learner made or applied: changed when today's session took it right away, unchanged when today's session stays as it was (underway or done), so the change starts on the next study day. Null otherwise

chapterTitle.description: For a test-out, the chapter its lessons were skipped from when they all come from one

progress.description: Where the plan stands, with preparation and this week's gain

weekGain.description: Preparation gained since the start of the learner's week (Monday)

shortPlan.description: A test days away, planned day by day: which day today is (Day 1 of 3), what it's for, and the day of its short mock; null for any other plan

mockDate.description: The short mock's day; null when the last day is a light review

studiedToday.description: Any study time today; a buddy never naps on a day with study

suggestedGoal.description: A course the learner was taking before goals existed, offered as another goal to plan until it's answered

weeklyChallenge.description: The goal's next weekly checkpoint: a mock exam or a mixed challenge

planItemId.description: The challenge's plan item, which opens its intro before and on its day

checklist.description: Rehearsing the real exam day: keys ticked off on the device (a class test gets materials and sleep)

dayBefore.description: What the day before the test holds: light (a short review), mock (a class test's short mock), review (a full review of every topic in the test's format, the weakest first, in place of a short mock the learner's plan doesn't include), learn or learnAndMock (a test tomorrow: the topics that come up most, with or without the mock)

prepared.description: The learner did what their plan asked before today (a session, no lessons left from earlier days, most study days finished): say they prepared only when true

startDate.description: First day of a week at half the time

from.description: The day the week's checkpoint or mock is planned

to.description: A later day to take it, within a week

targetDate.description: The new date, or null for none

areas.description: Area names exactly as the plan lists them

parts.description: Some of `areas` narrowed to the part the learner named (biology and chemistry of a sciences area that also holds physics): only those skills get the focus. Omitted, each area keeps the part it had; an area without a part is focused whole

areas.description: Area names exactly as the plan lists them
Area names exactly as the plan lists them

oneOf.description: Brings these areas back to their usual place: skipped ones back in the plan, and ones given less time (`reduceAreas`) their usual time

areas.description: Area names exactly as the plan lists them

oneOf.description: Less time for these areas, which stay in the plan (the learner wants less of them): they count half, so their depth and their share of the days go to the other areas first. A focus on one, or `restoreAreas`, gives it its usual time again

activities.description: Language practice to leave out of lessons, such as writing

cadence.description: When an exam's written tests (a redação, a discursive test) are practiced: weekly (the default, spaced practice), biweekly (every other week and the final stretch) or finalWeeks (only the final weeks before the exam, which needs a date). The total practice stays the same

areas.description: Area names exactly as the plan lists them

start.description: pastBasics: these areas start past their foundations, at their higher bands (the learner said their lessons are too basic). basics: they start from their foundations again

name.description: The part as the learner says it, such as "Biologia e Química"

skillIds.description: The area's skills in the part, from the plan's graph

dailyMinutes.description: Minutes a day for this goal

details.description: What onboarding understood: exam, date, target score, course or position, level, reason, purpose, role

language.description: The language the learner studies in

bearerAuth.description: Zoonk session token sent in the Authorization header.
